tagline: Global leader in beverage alcohol, building iconic brands across spirits, beer, and wine
hero_kpi_rationale: The 28.1% operating margin reflects Diageo's financial discipline and effective operational management in an inflationary environment. This indicator is structural and comparable, demonstrating the ability to convert revenue into operating profit.
company_description: Diageo plc, together with its subsidiaries, engages in the production, marketing, and distribution of alcoholic beverages in North America, Europe, the Asia Pacific, Latin America and Caribbean, and Africa. It offers beer, scotch, gin, vodka, rum, liqueur, raki, wine, Irish and Canadian whisky, US and Indian whisky, Chinese whisky, cachaça, tequila, brandy, and Chinese white spirit beverages. The company also provides ready-to-drink and non-alcoholic beverages. Its principal brands include Johnnie Walker, Don Julio, Guinness, Crown Royal, Smirnoff, Baileys, Captain Morgan, Casamigos, Shui Jing Fang, and McDowell's. The company was formerly known as Guinness plc and changed its name to Diageo plc in February 1998. The company was incorporated in 1886 and is headquartered in London, the United Kingdom.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: The portion of revenue that remains after paying production costs.
kpis.description: Gross margin stands at 59.6%, slightly improved versus last year thanks to effective price and cost management.
kpis.signal: Gross margin stability despite cost inflation.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: The percentage of revenue that becomes profit before tax.
kpis.description: Operating margin remains stable at 28.1%, reflecting discipline in operating expenses.
kpis.signal: Operating margin maintained despite growing investments.

kpis.name: R&D Investment (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: What the company spends on research and development relative to its revenue.
kpis.description: R&D spending represents 1.2% of revenue, slightly up, primarily focused on product innovation and packaging.
kpis.signal: Modest R&D, consistent with a brand-led rather than technology model.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Money invested in plants, machinery or buildings.
kpis.description: Capex was $900 million, up 12%, supported by energy efficiency and capacity projects.
kpis.signal: Capex rising to modernize production sites.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of people employed by the company.
kpis.description: Total headcount is 27,500 employees, down 2%, tied to efficiency gains and digital transformation.
kpis.signal: Headcount reduction in an optimization context.

kpis.name: Organic Net Sales Growth
kpis.explanation: Measures Diageo's sales growth excluding FX and acquisitions, showing true performance.

kpis.name: Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Diageo's net revenue, the total money earned from selling its alcoholic beverages after deductions.

kpis.name: Premium+ Net Sales Share
kpis.explanation: Measures the share of high-end spirits sales, showing whether Diageo is selling more lucrative premium products.

kpis.name: North America Op Margin
kpis.explanation: Measures the profit percentage generated by sales in North America after operating expenses.

kpis.name: Net Debt / EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Measures how many times Diageo's net debt could be repaid by annual earnings. Indicates financial health.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of 14.8064 GBp in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of 2.298 billion GBp in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 97.6% in the latest year.

risks.title: Risk of Fraud and Financial Statement Manipulation
risks.summary: Auditors identified a risk that Diageo's management could manipulate the accounts, for example by removing expenses to improve reported results or biasing accounting estimates.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in the middle of the report, in the audit section; language used is moderate ('principal risks were related to posting inappropriate journal entries'); stable risk identified every year by auditors; the regulatory/fraud category receives a heavy weighting in the evaluation.

risks.title: Non-Compliance with Anti-Bribery and Tax Laws
risks.summary: Diageo operates in many countries and must comply with strict anti-bribery and payroll tax laws. A failure could materially impact its accounts.
risks.score_rationale: Positioned in the middle of the report in the audit responsibilities section; language is factual but serious ('non-compliance might have a material effect on the financial statements'); stable recurring risk; the regulatory category has heavy weighting.

risks.title: Revenue Decline Over Two Consecutive Fiscal Years
risks.summary: Diageo's total sales have declined each year since 2022, from nearly $30 billion to less than $28 billion, signaling growing pressure on demand or product competitiveness.
risks.score_rationale: Visible directly in the consolidated income statement at the end of the financial section; language is factual (figures: $29,751M in 2022, $28,270M in 2023, $27,891M in 2024); risk trend is rising as the sales decline accelerates; competition category, moderate weighting.

risks.title: Rising Finance Costs Weighing on Profitability
risks.summary: Interest and financial expenses paid by Diageo are rising year over year, reducing earnings available to shareholders in a high interest rate environment.
risks.score_rationale: Data presented in the consolidated income statement, financial section; finance costs rose from $1,217M to $1,285M in two years, trend rising; language is factual but the impact on pre-tax profit is direct and measurable; capital category, moderate weighting.

risks.title: Decline in Net Income Attributable to Shareholders
risks.summary: Net income attributable to Diageo's shareholders has been steadily declining since 2022, which could weigh on the share price and the group's ability to pay dividends.
risks.score_rationale: Positioned in the consolidated income statement, financial section; attributable income fell from $4,280M to $3,870M in two years, a 9.6% decline; rising risk trend; capital category, moderate weighting.

risks.title: Risk of Exceeding Audit Tenure with the Same Firm
risks.summary: PricewaterhouseCoopers has audited Diageo without interruption for 9 years, which may raise questions about the firm's independence and the quality of accounts control.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned at the end of the audit report; language is neutral and informative ('period of total uninterrupted engagement is 9 years'); stable risk as the situation is known and regulated; regulatory category, heavy weighting but limited impact here.

ai_positioning.summary: Diageo does not mention any significant artificial intelligence strategy or initiative in its financial documents. The company focuses on brands, distribution and consumer experience.
evidence: No mention of AI or machine learning in the 2024 annual report
No references to AI tools in supply chain management or marketing
Absence of KPIs related to AI adoption or technological innovation
